coverage: All surviving play text and epilogue across the seventeen source reading units in original-en and modern-en. Opening Act 1 scene 1 is absent; several later scenes share units and titles are wrong. Publishing footer text is excluded. Coverage is not claimed for absent text.

entities.name: Rosalind
entities.body: Duke Senior’s daughter and Celia’s cousin; the play’s central heroine.

snapshots.body: Duke Senior’s daughter, disguised as the young man Ganymede.
Orlando’s bride and Duke Senior’s daughter; formerly disguised as Ganymede.

entities.name: Orlando
entities.body: Sir Rowland de Boys’s youngest son and Oliver’s brother.

snapshots.body: Rosalind’s bridegroom, Sir Rowland de Boys’s youngest son.

entities.name: Celia
entities.body: Duke Frederick’s daughter and Rosalind’s close friend and cousin.

snapshots.body: Rosalind’s cousin, traveling in disguise as Aliena.
Oliver’s bride and Rosalind’s cousin; formerly disguised as Aliena.

entities.name: Duke Senior
entities.body: Rosalind’s father, driven into exile by his younger brother Frederick.

snapshots.body: Rosalind’s father, restored to his dukedom after exile.

entities.name: Duke Frederick
entities.body: Celia’s father and Duke Senior’s younger brother, who has taken over the dukedom.

snapshots.body: Celia’s father and Duke Senior’s brother, who has renounced his rule for a religious life.

entities.name: Touchstone
entities.body: The court fool who is close to Celia and Rosalind.

snapshots.body: The court fool and Audrey’s bridegroom.

entities.name: Le Beau
entities.body: A courtier in Duke Frederick’s household.

entities.name: Charles
entities.body: Duke Frederick’s wrestler.

entities.name: Sir Rowland de Boys
entities.body: The late father of Oliver, Jaques de Boys and Orlando.

entities.name: Jaques
entities.body: The melancholy courtier living in exile with Duke Senior.

entities.name: Jaques de Boys
entities.body: Sir Rowland’s second son, brother to Oliver and Orlando.

entities.name: Amiens
entities.body: A courtier and singer among Duke Senior’s companions in exile.

entities.name: Hisperia
entities.body: An attendant of Celia at Duke Frederick’s court.

entities.name: Adam
entities.body: The elderly servant of the de Boys family, devoted to Orlando.

entities.name: Oliver
entities.body: Sir Rowland de Boys’s eldest son and Orlando’s elder brother.

snapshots.body: Celia’s bridegroom and Orlando’s elder brother.

entities.name: Corin
entities.body: An elderly shepherd in the Forest of Arden.

entities.name: Silvius
entities.body: The young shepherd in love with Phebe.

snapshots.body: The shepherd paired with Phebe at the wedding.

entities.name: Phebe
entities.body: The shepherdess loved by Silvius.

snapshots.body: The shepherdess who agrees to marry Silvius.

entities.name: Jane Smile
entities.body: The countrywoman whom Touchstone recalls as an old love.

entities.name: Audrey
entities.body: The countrywoman courted by Touchstone.

snapshots.body: Touchstone’s bride, a countrywoman of Arden.

entities.name: Sir Oliver Martext
entities.body: The village vicar whom Touchstone asks to marry him to Audrey.

entities.name: William
entities.body: The young countryman who is in love with Audrey.

entities.name: The first exiled lord
entities.body: One of Duke Senior’s companions in the Forest of Arden.

entities.name: The second exiled lord
entities.body: One of Duke Senior’s companions in the Forest of Arden.

entities.name: The first court lord
entities.body: A lord attending Duke Frederick at his court.

entities.name: The second court lord
entities.body: A lord attending Duke Frederick at his court.

entities.name: The lord returning from the hunt
entities.body: One of the forest lords whom Jaques meets after the deer hunt.

entities.name: The first page
entities.body: One of the Duke’s pages who sings for Touchstone and Audrey.

entities.name: The second page
entities.body: One of the Duke’s pages who sings for Touchstone and Audrey.

entities.name: Corin’s employer
entities.body: The owner of the cottage, pasture and flock that are offered for sale.

entities.name: The old religious man
entities.body: The religious man whom Frederick meets at the edge of the forest.

entities.name: The uncle in Ganymede’s story
entities.body: The religious uncle whom Rosalind, as Ganymede, credits with teaching her about love.

entities.name: The magician in Rosalind’s story
entities.body: The magician whom Rosalind claims to have known since childhood.

entities.name: The lover in Ganymede’s story
entities.body: The man whom Rosalind, as Ganymede, claims to have cured of love.

entities.name: Hymen
entities.body: The figure of the god of marriage who presides over the couples’ union.

entities.name: Ovid
entities.body: The Roman poet whose exile is invoked by Touchstone.

entities.name: Pythagoras
entities.body: The Greek philosopher associated with the transmigration of souls, invoked in Rosalind’s joke.

entities.name: Cleopatra
entities.body: The queen of Egypt invoked as an example of majesty in the poem about Rosalind.

entities.name: Lucretia
entities.body: The Roman woman traditionally celebrated for chastity, invoked in the poem about Rosalind.

entities.name: Christopher Marlowe
entities.body: The poet of Hero and Leander, addressed as the dead shepherd when Phebe quotes him.

entities.name: Julius Caesar
entities.body: The Roman general whose boast about coming, seeing and conquering Rosalind quotes.

entities.name: Fortune
entities.body: Luck personified as a woman distributing gifts from her wheel.

entities.name: Nature
entities.body: Nature personified as the giver of physical qualities, contrasted with Fortune.

entities.name: The Fates
entities.body: The classical powers governing destiny, called the Destinies.

entities.name: Hercules
entities.body: The mythological hero of extraordinary strength, invoked at the wrestling match.

entities.name: Cupid
entities.body: The classical god of love.

entities.name: Juno
entities.body: The Roman goddess of marriage, associated with Jupiter.

entities.name: Jupiter
entities.body: The Roman king of the gods, also called Jove.

entities.name: Ganymede in mythology
entities.body: The Trojan youth who serves as Jupiter’s cupbearer.

entities.name: Adam in the Bible
entities.body: The first man in the biblical creation story, invoked in Duke Senior’s reflection on exile.

entities.name: Diana
entities.body: The classical goddess of hunting and chastity, also invoked as the moon.

entities.name: Helen of Troy
entities.body: The woman celebrated for beauty in Trojan legend, invoked in the poem about Rosalind.

entities.name: Atalanta
entities.body: The swift runner and huntress of Greek myth, invoked in comparisons with Rosalind and Orlando.

entities.name: Gargantua
entities.body: The giant in Rabelais’s stories, invoked for the size of his mouth.

entities.name: Judas Iscariot
entities.body: The biblical betrayer of Jesus, invoked in Celia’s jokes about hair and kisses.

entities.name: Troilus
entities.body: The Trojan lover invoked in Rosalind’s argument about dying for love.

entities.name: Leander
entities.body: The mythological lover who swims the Hellespont to visit Hero.

entities.name: Hero
entities.body: The priestess at Sestos loved by Leander in classical legend.

entities.name: Venus
entities.body: The Roman goddess of love.

entities.name: The phoenix
entities.body: The legendary bird evoked as an emblem of rarity in Rosalind’s teasing.

entities.name: God
entities.body: The Christian deity invoked in prayers and oaths.

entities.name: The wrestlers’ father
entities.body: The elderly father of the three young men who wrestle Charles.

entities.name: The three brothers
entities.body: The three brothers who take on Charles in the wrestling match.

entities.name: Oliver in the song
entities.body: The Oliver addressed in the song fragment Touchstone quotes to the vicar.
